passage_summary: Judges survives in two notably distinct Greek recensions, conventionally the A-text (Alexandrinus and allies) and the B-text (Vaticanus and allies); Rahlfs prints both in parallel for much of Judges. At 5:1 the divergences are minor, chiefly orthographic in the proper names, but the A/B split is real.

witnesses.character: Representative of the B-text of Judges, often associated with a kaige-type revision.
Sinaiticus is lacunose for most of the Octateuch including Judges; it does not survive here.
Representative of the A-text of Judges, generally closer to the Hexaplaric/Origenic tradition.

readings.description: A-text form of the patronymic, closer to MT Abinoam.
B-text spelling with iota, an orthographic variant of the same name.

divergences.significance: Purely orthographic; reflects the divergent transliteration habits of the A- and B-traditions rather than a substantive variant.

readings.description: Both uncials agree on the standard transliteration; minor spelling differences (single vs. double consonant) are reported in some witnesses but not weighty.

divergences.significance: No substantive divergence; noted only because Brooke-McLean records minor orthographic variation in the minuscule tradition.

assessment.synthesis: Judges 5:1 is a place where the A/B recensional split of Judges is visible only at the level of name-spelling. The content of the verse — Deborah and Barak singing on that day — is uniform across the extant uncials. Sinaiticus is not available as a witness here.
verify_against: Rahlfs-Hanhart (which prints A and B texts of Judges in parallel)
Brooke-McLean, The Old Testament in Greek, vol. I part 4 (Joshua, Judges, Ruth)
